idiom_name: sealed trait OrderEvent + final case class events + match (warning on non-exhaustive)
implementation_notes: Scala's algebraic-data-type style is the idiomatic realization: a sealed trait with case-class events gives an exhaustively matchable closed set, and reactions are functions in an explicit handler list or a small dispatcher - the compiler warns on non-exhaustive matches, so adding an event type surfaces every dispatcher that must be updated. Keep the handler list explicit and dispatch at the unit-of-work boundary for synchronous, in-transaction reactions.
pitfalls: Case-class events are shallow-immutable: a List field leaks a mutable collection into handlers; use immutable collections and expose vals only.
A Map[Class[_], ...] registry matches the runtime class only, so an event extending another event is silently routed to nobody unless traits are matched explicitly.

variants.name: Pekko/Akka EventStream (classic event bus)
variants.implementation_notes: In actor-system codebases the bus already exists: Pekko's (formerly Akka's) EventStream is a subchannel-classified event bus where subscribers register by class - including a superclass, so classOf[DomainEvent] receives every subtype - and publish fans out to ActorRefs, with subscribers removed automatically when their actor terminates. Choose it when the model already lives in an actor system and reactions are actors; a plain Scala application should prefer the sealed-ADT dispatcher rather than pull in an ActorSystem.
variants.code_sketch:
case class OrderPlaced(orderId: Long) extends DomainEvent

system.eventStream.subscribe(listenerRef, classOf[OrderPlaced])
system.eventStream.publish(OrderPlaced(orderId))
pitfalls: The event stream is local to the actor system: it does not distribute across cluster nodes, so cross-node reactions need cluster pub-sub or a broker.
Subscribing by class fans out over a hierarchy, so a listener registered for a broad supertype receives far more than it expects and must filter.
